title: DuckWild Wildlife Tracking System
alt: Prototype wildlife tracking node with camera and LoRa mesh networking
description: A low-power wildlife monitoring system that uses on-device computer vision and a LoRa mesh network to detect and identify animals without relying on cellular or Wi-Fi connectivity.

sections.title: Project Overview
sections.body: DuckWild is an off-grid wildlife monitoring system that combines edge AI and long-range mesh networking. The system uses a Raspberry Pi, motion sensing, and an infrared camera to detect animals, identify species locally, and transmit lightweight data packets over a LoRa mesh network using the ClusterDuck Protocol. The goal is to enable wildlife tracking in remote environments without relying on cellular, Wi-Fi, or manual SD card retrieval.

sections.title: The Problem
items: Traditional wildlife cameras store images locally, requiring physical retrieval
Cellular models are expensive and unreliable in remote areas
Most capture far more useless data than actionable insight
DuckWild filters at the edge—sending structured data instead of raw images

items.label: Edge node
items.value: Raspberry Pi + IR camera + PIR motion sensor

items.label: Networking
items.value: LoRa radio (SX1262) using the ClusterDuck Protocol

items.label: Mesh routing
items.value: Packets hop node-to-node until reaching a gateway (PapaDuck)

sections.title: What We’ve Built So Far
items: Python-based ClusterDuck implementation for Raspberry Pi
Successful serialization and transmission of ClusterDuck-compatible packets over LoRa
Working computer vision pipeline running fully on-device
~94% species classification accuracy on a real trail-camera dataset
Power-aware design decisions keeping average consumption under ~5W

sections.title: Key Technical Decisions
items: Reimplemented ClusterDuck in Python instead of modifying upstream C++ for maintainability and reuse
Dropped hardware AI accelerators due to power cost with little benefit for solar operation
Motion-triggered, event-driven inference so AI only runs when needed

sections.title: My Contributions
items: Helped design the system state machine and overall software flow
Integrated motion sensing, camera capture, and AI inference
Contributed to ClusterDuck packet handling and Raspberry Pi compatibility
Made power and architecture decisions based on real measurements

sections.title: Current Focus / What’s Next
items: Full integration of AI pipeline + mesh networking
Solar and battery system bring-up
Weatherproof enclosure design
Long-range field testing with multiple nodes
Public demo video + open-source release

sections.title: Why This Project Matters
sections.body: DuckWild shows how embedded systems, networking, and AI intersect in the real world. It’s not about maximizing benchmarks—it’s about making technology usable where infrastructure doesn’t exist.
